d: Emotes are character animations used through chat commands, or accessing the emotes menu.
h:
Emotes are expressive character animations that are accessible by using chat commands ("/e cheer") or by accessing the emotes menu on the top right of any game. All users have access to default emotes, such as dance, point, and cheer. Additional avatar emotes can be purchased and equipped from the Marketplace.

In your game, you can perform the following emote customizations:

  • Open and close a user's emotes menu programmatically.
  • Add or remove emotes options from a user's menu.
  • Disable access to the menu.
  • Play an emote, targeting a specific user character.

Emotes menu

You can open and close a user's emote menu manually, customize the menu to display specific emotes, or disable the menu completely.

Open and close

To manually open or close a player's emote menu, call GuiService:SetEmotesMenuOpen() with a boolean value of true or false.

The following code sample will open the emotes menu for the user:

-- Open the emote Menu
local GuiService = game:GetService("GuiService")
GuiService:SetEmotesMenuOpen(true)

If you need to detect whether the emotes menu is open, call GuiService:GetEmotesMenuOpen(). This returns a boolean indicating the menu's current state.

Add and remove emotes

Customize the emote menu by setting emotes from the catalog and then equipping emotes to a Humanoid. Set emotes with the HumanoidDescription:SetEmotes() method and equip up to 8 emotes to the emotes menu using HumanoidDescription:SetEquippedEmotes().

Use the following code sample in a LocalScript within the StarterCharacterScripts folder to set and equip emotes in your game:

local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local humanoid = Players.LocalPlayer.Character.Humanoid
local humanoidDescription = humanoid.HumanoidDescription

-- Set custom emotes within a table
local emoteTable = {
  ["Hello"] = {3576686446},
  ["Stadium"] = {3360686498},
  ["Tilt"] = {3360692915},
  ["Shrug"] = {3576968026},
  ["Salute"] = {3360689775},
  ["Point"] = {3576823880}
}
humanoidDescription:SetEmotes(emoteTable)

-- Equip emotes in a specific order
local equippedEmotes = {"Hello", "Stadium", "Tilt", "Shrug", "Salute", "Point"}
humanoidDescription:SetEquippedEmotes(equippedEmotes)

Key names, such as "Shrug" or "Salute" are customizable and will appear to the player as written. Emotes will also show up in the order they were set, starting at the top of the wheel and continuing clockwise.

Disable

Disable the emotes menu with StarterGui:SetCoreGuiEnabled(). Disabling the emotes menu will not prevent emotes from being performed with a chat command.

The following sample code will disable the emotes menu:

local StarterGui = game:GetService("StarterGui")
StarterGui:SetCoreGuiEnabled(Enum.CoreGuiType.EmotesMenu, false)

In addition to disabling the menu, you can disable loading of user-owned emotes by setting the StarterPlayer.UserEmotesEnabled property within StarterPlayer ⟩ Character to false. This specific property can only be set in Studio and cannot be set by scripts.

Play emotes

To manually play an emote that a character has in its HumanoidDescription, call Humanoid:PlayEmote(), passing the string name of the emote. This call will return true to indicate that the emote was played successfully, or false otherwise.

Use the following code sample to play the Shrug emote:

local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local humanoid = Players.LocalPlayer.Character.Humanoid

humanoid:PlayEmote("Shrug")

kid.simple: Emotes are short animations like waving, dancing, or cheering. Players use them by typing chat commands like `/e cheer` or by opening the emotes menu. This page shows how to open or close that menu with a script, choose which emotes appear in it, turn the menu off, and make a character play an emote.
kid.analogy: The emotes menu is like a wheel of stickers you can slap on your character. You, the game maker, can choose which stickers go on the wheel or take the wheel away.
keyPoints: Every player gets default emotes like dance, point, and cheer. More can be bought on the Marketplace.
Open or close the menu with `GuiService:SetEmotesMenuOpen(true)` or `false`, and check it with `GetEmotesMenuOpen()`.
Use `HumanoidDescription:SetEmotes()` to set which emotes a character has, as a table of name to asset ID.
Use `SetEquippedEmotes()` to put up to 8 emotes on the wheel. They appear in order, starting at the top and going clockwise.
The names you choose, like "Shrug", are exactly what players see.
Turn the menu off with `StarterGui:SetCoreGuiEnabled(Enum.CoreGuiType.EmotesMenu, false)`. Chat commands still work.
To stop players' own bought emotes from loading, uncheck `UserEmotesEnabled` in StarterPlayer in Studio. Scripts cannot change it.
Play an emote by name with `Humanoid:PlayEmote()`. The API reference says to use `PlayEmoteAsync()` for new work.

terms.emote: A short character animation used to express yourself, like a wave or a dance.
terms.emotes menu: The wheel of emotes players open from the top right of the screen.
terms.chat command: Text typed in chat that does something, like `/e dance`.
terms.HumanoidDescription: An object listing a character's look and animations, including its emotes.
terms.equip: Put an emote onto the wheel so players can pick it. The wheel holds up to 8.
terms.asset ID: The number that identifies an item on Roblox, like `3576686446` for the Hello emote.
terms.clockwise: The direction a clock's hands move: top, then right, then bottom, then left.

example.title: Set up a custom emote wheel and play one
example.code:
local character = script.Parent
local humanoid = character:WaitForChild("Humanoid")
local description = humanoid:WaitForChild("HumanoidDescription")

-- Name shown in the menu = list of emote asset IDs
local emoteTable = {
	["Hello"] = {3576686446},
	["Shrug"] = {3576968026},
	["Salute"] = {3360689775},
}
description:SetEmotes(emoteTable)

-- Put them on the wheel in this order (top, then clockwise)
description:SetEquippedEmotes({"Hello", "Shrug", "Salute"})

-- Play the Shrug emote after 2 seconds
task.wait(2)
local ok, result = pcall(function()
	return humanoid:PlayEmoteAsync("Shrug")
end)
print("Shrug played:", ok and result)
explain: This LocalScript is copied into each new character, so `script.Parent` is the character.
We find the character's `HumanoidDescription`, which holds its emotes.
`SetEmotes` gives the character three emotes with friendly names and their asset IDs.
`SetEquippedEmotes` puts them on the emote wheel in that order.
After 2 seconds, `PlayEmoteAsync("Shrug")` plays it. It is wrapped in `pcall` because it errors if the emote name is not found.

watchOut: Trying to equip more than 8 emotes. The wheel only holds 8.
Playing an emote name the character does not have. It errors, so set it with `SetEmotes` first and use `pcall`.
Thinking that hiding the menu blocks emotes. Players can still use chat commands like `/e dance`.
Trying to change `UserEmotesEnabled` in a script. It only works when set in Studio.
